summary: chain-analyze ships a dist-only DES-decrypt-and-exec loader that runs attacker-controlled JavaScript on module load
details: The published dist bundles (dist/sigchain-js.cjs.js, dist/sigchain-js.esm.js, dist/sigchain-js.umd.js) contain an added code path not present in the src/ tree. On module load, readRSAFromPackage() reads the consuming project's package.json via process.cwd() + fs.readFileSync and extracts an 'rsa' field. decryptToken() DES-decrypts that field using a `desKey` imported from the sibling dependency chain-manager. The plaintext is then executed by spawning `child_process.spawn('node', [], {...})` and writing the decrypted string to the child's stdin, running arbitrary JavaScript on the installer's host. The payload is absent from src/ and appears only in the compiled dist bundles, indicating a tampered build. Package metadata is inconsistent with the advertised identity: the package presents as a Theta SDK (chain-analyze), but the shipped bundles are named sigchain-js.*, package.json declares main as dist/chain-analyze.cjs.js which is not present in the tarball, the companion chain-manager dependency is used only to supply the DES key, and axios is pinned to a non-existent version 1.18.1. Any consumer that require()s or import()s this package triggers execution of the DES-decrypted payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
